easy.def: To do what you are told.
examples: My dog will obey when I say "sit."
We obey the school rules.
The horse obeys the rider.

more.def: To do what a person, rule, or law tells you to do.
examples: Drivers must obey the traffic signs.
Soldiers must obey their orders.
The well-trained dog obeyed every command.

easy.def: A thing you can see and touch.
examples: A ball is a round object.
What is that object in the sky?
Put each object in the box.

more.def: A thing that you can see and touch, but that is not alive.
examples: There was a shiny object at the bottom of the pond.
Sharp objects should be kept away from babies.
A telescope helps you see objects in space.

easy.def: A reason you give for not liking something.
examples: I have no objection.
Her objection was that it was too late.
Does anyone have an objection?

more.def: A statement saying that you do not agree with or like something.
examples: Dad had no objection to our going to the park.
The class raised an objection to the new rule.
Her main objection was that the price was too high.
We observe the ants as they work.
We observe the moon at night.
The cat observes the bird.

more.def: To watch someone or something closely in order to learn about it.
examples: The class observed how the caterpillar changed over two weeks.
Doctors observed the patient overnight.
If you observe the sky tonight, you may see a comet.
The answer is obvious.
It was obvious she was sad.
An obvious mistake.
The answer was obvious to everyone.
It was obvious that the dog was happy.
The hole in the roof was an obvious problem.

easy.def: In a way that is easy to see.
examples: He was obviously sad.
It was obviously broken.
She was obviously tired.

more.def: In a way that is easy for everyone to see or understand.
examples: She was obviously excited about the trip.
The window was obviously broken.
He obviously loved his dog.
